r.name: Monarch's Way
r.description: approximate route of Charles II's escape

r.name: Forest of Mercia Way
r.description: Bentley Lane Park to Cannock Chase along the Wyrley and Essington Canal

r.name: Two Saints Way
r.description: Two Saints Way - Chester Cathedral to/from Lichfield Cathedral. In the late Middle Ages a steady stream of pilgrims walked this way – both housing shrines to two game-changing Mercian saints in the 7th century - St Werburgh and St Chad

r.name: Staffordshire Way (Cannock Chase South)
r.description: Staffordshire Way, part Cannock Chase - south

r.name: Barrow Hill Geological Walk
r.description: Self-guided geological walk around Barrow Hill with particular places or features of interest being identified. The reserve may be entered from several access points . The sequence of numbering starts from Vicarage Lane but as the stops are self contained

r.name: Dudley Geological Heritage Trail
r.description: Discover millions of years of geological history along this heritage trail. This tour allows you to experience Dudley’s fascinating history through its buildings.

r.name: Rushall Junction to Ryders Green Locks
r.description: This route features an unusual aqueduct; one of the few examples of a canal crossing over a railway. Distance: 7.5 miles/12 km (approx) Duration: 1 hour 15 min (approx)

r.name: Dudley Port Circular
r.description: Follow The Gower Branch, then turn right back onto The Old Main Line. For a more challenging route, continue along The New Main Line and cross at Bromford Junction. Take the ramp access to The Old Main Line and double back, crossing Blakeley Hall Bridge.

r.name: Neptune Health Park Walk
r.description: The Neptune is a circular 4 mile walk along the quiet New Main Line, and Old Main Line Canals. It also makes an excellent cycle route, and finishes next to a pub. Distance: 4 miles/6.5km (approx) Duration: 1 hour 20 mins (approx)

r.name: Rowley Hills Geology Trail
r.description: A self-guided circular walk around the summit and the northern slope of Rowley Hills, taking in 15 points of interest. Not suitable for disabled/buggies due to rough ground, steep slopes and steps.

r.name: Sheepwash Park Circular Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest site. Route circles the largest forest park in the Black Country- being a reclaimed former brick works and waste tip. Difficulty: Medium due to unsurfaced paths Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: West Bromwich to Oldbury Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route passes 500+yr old Oak House and along the banks of the River Tame. Difficulty: Easy Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Galton Valley Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route follows what was once the longest earthwork in the world and under Telford's Galton Bridge. Difficulty: Medium due to unsurfaced paths and steps Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Bilston to Loxdale Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route passes 15th century Greyhound & Punchbowl pub and Bradley Arm which is topped up by pumping water out of disused mines. Difficulty: Medium due to slopes Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Moorcroft Wood/ Walsall Canal Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route crosses Moorcroft Wood- a former coal/ iron mine now mixed wetland habitat; and along the 1786 Walsall Canal Difficulty: Hard due to slopes/ dirt paths Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Dudley Public Art Heritage Trail (Wolverton Road Trail)
r.description: This tour allows you to experience Dudley’s fabulous pieces of public art from the past 200 years. You can walk the town centre & Priory Park trails together in ~1 hour. If you have more time divert for an extra hour via the Wolverton Road trail.

r.name: Dudley Architectural Heritage Trail
r.description: Experience Dudley's history through buildings charting its history from an 1100s market town to being dominated by coal/iron by the 17/1800s.

r.name: Sedgley Heritage Trail 1
r.operator: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council;Sedgley Local History Society
r.description: The Sedgley Heritage Trails introduce some of the present-day and historical features of Sedgley. Walk 1 (Short Walk – red) begins at All Saints’ Church and is about 2km (1.25 miles) on flat ground and pavements.

r.name: Sedgley Heritage Trail 2
r.operator: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council;Sedgley Local History Society
r.description: The Sedgley Heritage Trails introduce some of the present-day and historical features of Sedgley. Walk 2 (Long Walk – green) begins at St Andrew’s Church and is about 3km (1.9 miles) with an incline to Beacon Tower and some unpaved sections.

r.name: Black Country Canals: The Dudley & Stourbridge Ring
r.description: 'Circuit' of Canals surrounding Dudley & Stourbridge. Follow the fascinating network of junctions and branches through scenery varying from industrial warehouses to suprisingly secluded rural lengths.

r.name: Wren's Nest UNESCO Black Country Geopark Geotrail
r.description: Trail around highlights of the UNESCO Global Geopark through strata making up 1.3 million years of Earth's history- once a shallow sea bed, see evidence of volcanic eruptions and fossil beds. Quarried intensely, see evidence of such excavations throughout

r.name: Walsall Walk of Art
r.description: A specially designed circular canalside walk, starting from Walsall’s New Art Gallery, passing through changing landscapes. Distance: 4 miles/6.5 km(approx) Duration: 80 mins(approx)

r.name: Sneyd Junction to Cannock Extension Canal
r.description: A semi-rural route following the curves of the canal, until it opens out into parkland at the Cannock Extension. Distance: 5.5 miles/8.8 km (approx) Duration: 45 min (approx)

r.name: Wolverhampton Locks Walk
r.description: A short walk from the city centre, this linear walk follows the towpath, passing 21 locks, historic buildings and changing landscapes. Distance: 2 miles/3.2 km(approx) Duration: 40 mins(approx)

r.name: Sneyd Junction to Pudding Green Junction
r.description: Canalside route passing through the heartlands of the industrial Black Country. Decends using the Walsall locks then rises at Ryders Green Locks. Distance: 10 miles/16 km (approx) Duration: 90 min (approx)

r.name: Sneyd Junction to Horseley Fields Junction
r.description: Canalside route following the Wyrley & Essington, taking New Cross Bridge, where the towpath changes to the other side of the canal. Distance: 6 miles/9.6 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Factory Junction to Ladywood Junction
r.description: Cycle along The New Main Line and follow the signs for The National Cycle Route, which takes you to Ladywood Junction and on into Birmingham City Centre. Distance: 6 miles/10 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Forest of Mercia Timberland Trail (Long Route)
r.operator: Timberland Clothing Company;The Countryside Agency;Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council
r.description: 10-mile circular route based on PRoW and canal towpaths, which would've been used by local miners, iron workers, and farmers. Car Parking at start on Wood Lane.

r.name: ABCD Pub Heritage Trail
r.operator: Wolverhampton Museums (All Saints and Blakenhall Community Development [ABCD] scheme);The Campaign for Real Ale
r.description: A short guide to pub heritage in the All Saints & Blakenhall areas. The trail celebrates ABCD local pubs that are still open for business and also remembers some that have closed.

r.name: ABCD War Heritage Trail
r.operator: Wolverhampton Museums (All Saints and Blakenhall Community Development [ABCD] scheme);Walking for Health
r.description: A short guide to some of the First and Second World War heritage of the All Saints and the Blakenhall area. This trail explores historic Wolverhampton sites associated with the periods 1914-1918 and 1939-1945.

r.name: All Saints' Trail
r.operator: Wolverhampton Museums (All Saints and Blakenhall Community Development [ABCD] scheme);Walking for Health
r.description: Heritage trail around the large former Parish of All Saints along a route traditionally church members would walk to beat set points with canes (known as 'Beating the Bounds) This formed a mental map of the area when maps were rare.

r.name: Walk Tipton Heritage Trail
r.description: Heritage trail around Tipton, growing from a tiny hamlet into an industrial power of ironmaking, heavy engineering, and canals. It pioneered steam engines, built the 1st iron steamship- 1822, the world’s largest anchor- 1866, and Thunderbolt car- 1937.

r.name: Walk Wednesbury Heritage Trail
r.description: Heritage trail around Wednesbury, named after the Saxon god Woden, grew from a 10th c rural land into a major industrial hub. Globally known for pottery, enamelling & ironwork. Fortified by Ethelflaed, its rich history is now rediscovered via archaeology.

r.name: The Blakenhall Trail
r.operator: Wolverhampton Museums (All Saints and Blakenhall Community Development [ABCD] scheme);Walking for Health
r.description: Circular heritage trail of the Blakenhall area of Wolverhampton which accompanied the "Through the eyes of an apprentice" project. This trail explores historic sites, remarkable buildings and interesting landmarks.

r.name: Tettenhall Village Trail
r.description: The Tettenhall Trail takes you on a walk around the village pointing out some of its important buildings and historic sites. Due to the hilly nature, those with mobility issues are likely to find the trail difficult due to steep slopes and steps.

r.name: Northycote Farm to Moseley Old Hall Walk, Moseley Old Hall
r.description: Trace the footsteps of a king as you join up with the Monarch's Way in the West Midlands. This route runs along fairly flat, woodland paths that can become muddy, as well as grassy fields and made tracks.

r.name: BCN Walks- Titford Canal
r.description: The Titford Canal walk starts below the M5 at Oldbury Locks Junction, climbs Oldbury Locks, and finishes at Titford Pools. Built 1773-4, the pools are the BCN's highest point at 511ft and connect to the navigable Causeway Green and Portway branches.
